name: UNLV TAVR robot
full_name: UNLV robotic transcatheter delivery system for TAVR: four-tendon omnidirectional bending joint driving a commercial balloon catheter
group: Robotics and Healthcare Systems (RoboHS) Laboratory, Dept. of Mechanical Engineering, University of Nevada, Las Vegas (R. Qi [corresponding], H. S. Gallage, B. F. De Sousa, B. I. Chesnik, C. G. Brownstein, A. Paul) (gallage2025_design title page)
versions: single version (gallage2025_design, arXiv 2506.12082v1, 9 Jun 2025, one-page-body short paper); 'an advancement over' the two-tendon mitral-valve delivery design of Nayar, Qi and Desai 2022 (ref. [3], Sec. I; Georgia Tech, catalogue row gatech_tmvr_qi2023)
target_anatomy: transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), 'optimal commissural and coronary alignment' for aortic stenosis (Abstract; Sec. I); no phantom or vessel used
devices_driven: own omnidirectional bending joint (8 Nylon 6/6 rings, OD 7 mm, four 0.16 mm superelastic nitinol tendons 90 deg apart at 2.5 mm radius) actuating a commercial Edwards balloon catheter, 3.2 mm diameter, 130 cm (Sec. I, II)
n_dof_detail: tip bending in any direction through one constant-curvature section by paired tendon actuation (4 motors); advance and roll N.R. (Sec. II, Fig. 1)
translation_detail: tendon/tip-actuation: four Pololu DC gear motors with pulleys pull the tendons, opposing tendons pull and release equal lengths (Sec. II, Fig. 1); catheter advance N.R.
rotation_detail: N.R. (bending plane set by the tendon pairs; no roll axis described)
device_range: joint OD 7 mm; balloon catheter 3.2 mm x 130 cm (Sec. I)
footprint_mm: actuation system 183 x 80 x 38 mm (Sec. II, Fig. 1)
validation_detail: bench: motion validation of the joint, about 90 deg bend in both directions in the horizontal plane and an omnidirectional bend shown in photos (Sec. II, Fig. 2a-c); no phantom ('future work: patient-specific phantoms', Sec. III); trial counts N.R.
key_numbers: maximum bending angle about 90 deg (Sec. II, III); joint OD 7 mm; actuation unit 183 x 80 x 38 mm; no accuracy, repeatability or time numbers
sim_model: none found (hysteresis and kinematic modelling are future work, Sec. III)

sources.title: Design and Development of a Robotic Transcatheter Delivery System for Aortic Valve Replacement

read_level_detail: full (the whole paper is one page of text; abstract level in the earlier REV4 §4)
notes: REV4 2026-11-23: included after the full assessment of the 19 candidates (REV4_19_candidates.md §7). Extremely short evidence base: a one-page arXiv short paper with a motion test and no vessel model; the row's phantom-free bench label is the paper's own 'preliminary experimental results'. Shares the TAVR-delivery theme of gatech_tmvr_qi2023 (same last author), a new institution and a different robot.
